name: ชีพจรลื่นหรือเร็ว
preview_text: ชีพจรเต้นเร็วลื่นเป็นสัญญาณที่ชัดเจนของเสมหะและความร้อน และเมื่อคุณรู้ว่าเสมหะร้อนสะสมอยู่ที่ใด การรักษาก็จะตรงไปตรงมา ผู้ป่วยส่วนใหญ่มองเห็นชีพจรของตนเอง...
categories: ["การวินิจฉัยชีพจร"]
conventional_description:
In conventional medicine, pulse assessment focuses on rate, rhythm, and volume - how fast the heart beats, whether the rhythm is regular, and whether the pulse feels strong or weak. A rapid pulse (tachycardia) may be caused by fever, infection, dehydration, anxiety, thyroid disorders, or cardiac conditions, and is investigated accordingly. The quality of “slipperiness” is not a recognized clinical sign, and no standard diagnostic framework links a smooth, rolling pulse sensation to internal phlegm or heat.
This means that many people with a slippery rapid pulse - and the underlying pattern of phlegm-heat - may have normal Western medical tests even though they feel unwell. Their digestive discomfort, heavy chest, or mental fog may be attributed to stress or functional disorders without a clear treatment pathway.
conventional_treatments: Because a slippery rapid pulse is not a Western diagnosis, there is no direct conventional treatment for it. If an underlying condition like infection, hyperthyroidism, or anxiety is identified, that condition is treated with antibiotics, antithyroid drugs, or anxiolytics. For functional digestive or respiratory symptoms, management may include antacids, bronchodilators, or lifestyle advice, but the unifying pattern of phlegm-heat is not addressed.
tcm_understanding:
In Chinese medicine, the pulse is a direct window into the flow of Qi and blood. A slippery pulse feels smooth and rounded, like little pearls rolling under the fingers, and it always indicates the presence of phlegm-dampness - a thick, sticky pathological fluid that can clog the body's channels. When the pulse is also rapid, it means there is heat, which accelerates the blood flow and often transforms that dampness into hot, irritating phlegm. Together, these two sensations create the classic slippery rapid pulse, a hallmark of phlegm-heat.
The location of the slippery rapid pulse on the wrist tells the practitioner which organ system is most affected. A strong slippery rapid pulse at the middle position points to the stomach and spleen, where phlegm is produced. At the front position, it suggests the lungs are clogged with hot phlegm. A deep, forceful quality throughout the whole pulse may indicate heat and accumulation in the intestines. If the pulse is especially full and slippery at the left front position, the heart and mind are being disturbed by phlegm-fire. This is why one pulse finding can map onto several different patterns - and why asking about your main symptoms is essential to pinpoint the correct treatment.
It's important to know that a slippery rapid pulse is always an excess condition. The body is grappling with something that shouldn't be there - too much phlegm, too much heat, or both. Treatment therefore focuses on clearing and draining, never on tonifying or supplementing, until the excess has been resolved. Once the phlegm-heat is gone, the pulse will naturally become softer, slower, and more balanced.
classical_quote: 「滑脉者，往来流利，如珠走盘。数脉者，一息六至。」
classical_translation: "A slippery pulse comes and goes smoothly, like pearls rolling on a plate. A rapid pulse exceeds four beats per breath cycle (six beats per breath)."
classical_source:
Mai Jing (Pulse Classic)  ,  Volume 4, Chapter 1 									·

tcm_diagnosis:
When a practitioner feels a pulse that is both slippery (rolling like pearls) and rapid (fast), it almost always signals a combination of phlegm-dampness and heat in the body. The next step is to ask about the symptoms that bother the person most, because the location of that phlegm-heat tells the full story. All the patterns that produce this pulse are excess conditions, so the pulse will feel forceful and strong under the fingers.
A person with phlegm-heat lodged in the stomach and spleen often complains of a heavy, bloated feeling in the upper abdomen, nausea, a sticky taste in the mouth, and a poor appetite. The tongue typically has a thick, greasy yellow coating, and the pulse feels especially slippery and rapid at the middle position of the wrist. This pattern is the most common cause of a slippery rapid pulse, because the middle burner is the hub where phlegm is produced.
When phlegm-heat moves upward into the lungs, the main complaints shift to the chest: a deep cough with thick, yellow sputum that is hard to expel, a sensation of fullness in the chest, and sometimes fever. The tongue is red with a yellow greasy coating, and the pulse is slippery and rapid, often more prominent at the front position on the right wrist, which corresponds to the lung. This pattern frequently follows a respiratory infection that was not fully cleared.
Bright Yang Fire in Stomach and Intestines is a severe form of heat and phlegm accumulating in the stomach and large intestine. The defining feature is constipation with dry, hard stools, along with abdominal distension, thirst, and a high fever.
The tongue is red with a dry, thick yellow coating, and the pulse is not only slippery and rapid but also large and forceful. It represents a deeper, more intense heat that has dried up fluids, creating a kind of phlegm-heat that clogs the bowels.
When phlegm-fire disturbs the mind and spirit, the person feels restless, irritable, and may have palpitations, insomnia, or a sense of oppression in the chest. In more intense cases, there can be mental confusion or manic behavior.
The tongue tip is especially red, with a yellow greasy coating, and the pulse is slippery and rapid, sometimes with a wiry quality. This pattern is less common but important to recognize because it affects emotional well-being so directly.

patterns.symptoms: ["Feeling of blockage and fullness in the upper abdomen", "Nausea or vomiting of sticky, bitter fluid", "Thick, yellow, greasy tongue coating", "Bitter taste in the mouth and bad breath", "Thirst with no desire to drink much", "Sensation of heat and heaviness in the body"]
patterns.worse_with: Greasy or fried foods, Alcohol and spicy foods, Overeating or late-night snacking, Hot, humid weather, Emotional stress and frustration
patterns.better_with: Light, bland foods (congee, steamed greens), Gentle daily movement (walking, qigong), Cooling foods like pear and radish, Avoiding overeating
patterns.why_this_happens: When thick, sticky Phlegm combines with Heat in the Stomach and Spleen, it creates a palpable disturbance in the blood flow. The Phlegm gives the pulse a smooth, rolling, bead-like quality, while the Heat accelerates the heart rate, producing the rapid beat. This slippery-rapid pulse is the direct reflection of the Phlegm-Heat mixture churning in the middle burner.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body, swollen, with a thick yellow greasy coating especially in the centre. Pulse: slippery (滑 huá) and rapid (数 shuò); may be wiry at the right middle position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Greasy, sweet, and heavy foods directly produce Dampness and Phlegm, while alcohol and spices add Heat, feeding the very Phlegm-Heat that creates the slippery-rapid pulse. Overeating overwhelms the Stomach and Spleen, causing food to stagnate and ferment into Phlegm-Heat. Light, bland foods and gentle movement help the Spleen transform and transport fluids, cutting off the source of Phlegm, while cooling foods and herbs clear the excess Heat, restoring a normal pulse.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Focus on light, easily digestible meals like congee and steamed vegetables. Strictly avoid greasy, fried, sweet, and dairy-heavy foods, as they generate more Phlegm. Cut out alcohol and spicy dishes that fuel Heat. Gentle daily movement like walking or qigong helps circulate Qi and transform Dampness.

patterns.symptoms: ["Cough with thick, sticky yellow or green sputum", "Chest tightness and shortness of breath", "Wheezing or gurgling sounds in the throat", "Fever or sensation of body heat"]
patterns.worse_with: Greasy or fried foods, Alcohol and spicy foods, Smoking or polluted air, Emotional stress and frustration, Overwork
patterns.better_with: Deep breathing, Warm water and light, non-greasy meals, Cooling herbal teas (e.g., chrysanthemum), Rest and avoiding overexertion
patterns.why_this_happens: When thick, hot phlegm clogs the Lungs, the body's Qi and blood flow become obstructed by sticky dampness. This creates a pulse that feels round and smooth like beads rolling under the fingers-the slippery quality. The trapped heat accelerates the heartbeat, making it rapid. The combination reflects the internal struggle between pathogenic heat and phlegm obstructing the Lung's descending function.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body, yellow greasy coating, possibly swollen at the front with red prickles. Pulse: slippery and rapid (滑数 huá shuò), strongest at the right cun (inch) position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Phlegm and heat are the core pathology. Greasy and dairy foods produce phlegm; spicy and hot foods generate heat. Smoking and polluted air directly damage the Lungs and create heat. Emotional stress stagnates Qi, which turns into fire and combines with phlegm. Overwork depletes Qi, weakening the body's ability to transform phlegm. Conversely, light, cooling foods and herbs clear heat and resolve phlegm; deep breathing helps disperse Lung Qi and expel phlegm; rest allows the body to recover and reduce heat.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid greasy, fried, and dairy foods that create more phlegm. Skip spicy and hot foods that add heat. Eat cooling, moistening foods like pears, radish, and bamboo shoots. Drink plenty of warm water to thin mucus. Avoid smoking and polluted air. Practice gentle deep-breathing exercises to support lung function.

patterns.why_this_happens: When intense heat builds up in the Stomach and Intestines, it dries up fluids and causes waste to stagnate. This internal excess creates a strong, forceful pulse that feels rapid because of the heat. The accumulation of turbid matter and undigested food gives the pulse a slippery, rolling quality, like pearls moving under the fingers.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with prickly thorns, thick yellow dry coating, possibly cracked. Pulse: deep, forceful, rapid, and slippery.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Spicy, greasy foods and alcohol pour fuel on the internal fire, increasing heat and drying up fluids, which worsens constipation and abdominal pain. Rest and a cool environment help the body conserve Yin and reduce heat agitation. Passing a bowel movement removes the accumulation of heat and waste from the intestines, directly relieving the pressure and heat that drive the rapid, slippery pulse.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid spicy, greasy, and fried foods, as well as alcohol and coffee, which add heat. Eat cooling, moistening foods like pear, watermelon, cucumber, and congee. Drink plenty of water to help soften stools. Rest and reduce stress to avoid aggravating internal fire.

patterns.why_this_happens: When emotional turmoil or dietary excess generates thick, sticky Phlegm and internal Heat, these two pathogenic factors can combine and rise to disturb the Heart. The Heat accelerates the flow of blood, making the pulse rapid, while the Phlegm creates a smooth, rolling sensation that is felt as slipperiness. This is why the pulse becomes both slippery and rapid, reflecting the agitation of the Heart spirit and the obstruction of Phlegm.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: Red body, swollen with red prickly tip, thick yellow greasy coating. Pulse: Slippery and rapid; the left Cun (Heart) position is full and overflowing, the right Guan (Spleen/Stomach) position is slippery.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Emotional upset stirs up Heart Fire, while greasy, heavy foods generate Phlegm-together they feed the root of this pattern. Cooling, calm practices and a light diet directly counter the Heat and Phlegm, allowing the spirit to settle and the pulse to return to normal.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid greasy, fried, and spicy foods, dairy, alcohol, and excessive caffeine-they create Phlegm and fan the flames of Heat. Eat cooling, light meals with plenty of vegetables like cucumber, celery, and water chestnut. A regular sleep schedule and calming practices like meditation or gentle yoga help settle the spirit.

faqs.question: What does a slippery rapid pulse actually feel like?
faqs.answer: A trained practitioner feels it as a smooth, rolling sensation under the fingertips - like a string of pearls passing by, or a small ball bearing rolling beneath the skin. At the same time, the pulse beats faster than normal, usually over 90 beats per minute. It feels full and forceful, not weak or faint.

faqs.question: Can I check my own pulse for slipperiness?
faqs.answer: It's very difficult to feel the slippery quality without training, because it requires a delicate touch and an understanding of what a normal pulse feels like for comparison. You can easily notice if your pulse is rapid by counting the beats, but the slippery sensation is best left to a qualified TCM practitioner. They will take your pulse on both wrists and at three different depths to get the full picture.

faqs.question: Is a slippery rapid pulse dangerous?
faqs.answer: The pulse itself is not dangerous; it's a sign that your body is dealing with phlegm and heat. However, the underlying pattern can be serious if left untreated, especially if it affects the heart or lungs. If you also have high fever, severe chest pain, mental confusion, or difficulty breathing, seek urgent medical care. Otherwise, TCM treatment can safely resolve the phlegm-heat.

faqs.question: What conditions can cause a slippery rapid pulse?
faqs.answer: In Chinese medicine, the same pulse can appear in digestive disorders (bloating, nausea, acid reflux), respiratory conditions (bronchitis, sinusitis with yellow phlegm), severe constipation with fever, and mental-emotional issues like anxiety, insomnia, or agitation. The common thread is always phlegm combined with heat. A TCM practitioner will use your tongue coating, symptoms, and the exact pulse position to determine which pattern is active.

faqs.question: Will my pulse change as I get better?
faqs.answer: Yes. As the phlegm clears and the heat cools, the pulse will gradually lose its slippery quality and slow down. You may notice that you feel less congested, your digestion improves, or your mind feels clearer before the pulse fully normalizes. The pulse is one of the last things to shift, so it serves as a reliable marker that the root imbalance has been resolved.

faqs.question: Can I combine TCM treatment with my regular medications?
faqs.answer: In most cases, yes. Herbal formulas that clear heat and transform phlegm are generally safe alongside conventional medications. However, if you take blood thinners like warfarin, certain herbs (such as Tao Ren in Wei Jing Tang) may increase bleeding risk. Always bring a full list of your medications to your TCM consultation and tell your doctor you are starting herbs.
